text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.08% today to close at $389.55, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 10.65% that began after crude oil prices tumbled hard last week. The immediate trigger is crude weakness: Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th—the first time since August—driven by statements from Trump suggesting the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon," which would ease geopolitical supply concerns that have kept oil prices elevated. Lower crude prices squeeze refinery margins because refiners buy oil at market rates and sell gasoline and diesel; when the raw material gets cheaper faster than finished products fall, their profit per barrel narrows.

The broader backdrop makes the selloff sharper: refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and gasoline inventories are already elevated at nearly 209 million barrels, suggesting demand may not be keeping pace with supply even at current prices. Combined with political uncertainty around Iran policy—Secretary of State Rubio said just yesterday that negotiations remain unproductive despite Trump's optimistic rhetoric—the market appears skeptical that oil prices will stabilize soon, leaving refinery economics under pressure.
